newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA MAIZE, BEET, OILSEED SOWINGS NEAR COMPLETE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA MAIZE, BEET, OILSEED SOWINGS NEAR COMPLETE.

text.p: Romania has almost completed sowing of maize, sugar beet and sunflower crops and expects warm weather to help produce a bumper wheat crop after last year's poor figures, a farm ministry official said on Tuesday.
Maize sowing was complete on 2.83 million ha, up from 1.93 million ha last week, Elena Fcoreico, an official with the ministry's press office, said by telephone.
Ministry data showed that maize had been sown on 90 percent of the planned area of 3.14 million hectares, up from 62 percent last Wednesday.
Sunflowers had been sown on 731,000 ha, or 93 percent of the planned 781,822 ha. Sugar beet sowing was complete on 134,000 ha, or 96 percent of the 138,401 ha planned.
"Wheat is growing fast, helped by recent warm weather which is forecast to continue throughout May," Fcoreico said.
The ministry has forecast a wheat crop of some 7.8 million tonnes against last year's disastrous 3.1 million tonnes.

Official forecasts put this year's exports at 1.5 million tonnes, which could bring Romania back among major players on world grain markets. Romania last exported 1.3 million tonnes from a good 1995 wheat crop.
Heavy rainfall last month had delayed farm work and hit sowing of maize, sugar beet and sunflowers. Reports said high soil humidity had favoured the growth of weeds on large areas.
Latest data showed herbicides were spread on 1.63 million ha of wheat, or 68 percent of the 2.37 million ha planted last autumn. This compared to 53 percent recorded last Wednesday.
"It's becoming increasingly difficult to spread herbicides on the rest of the area under wheat, because plants are now quite tall," Fcoreico said.
"We also expect a good barley crop this autumn, with herbicides spread on 300,000 ha, from the total of 415,000 ha planted."
